text:
infra-bot: ⚠️ Alert: NAT gateway (nat-3a) port utilization at 98% in eu-west-1 — high TIME_WAIT and socket churn detected
ashley: seeing lots of 502s from model-puller pods, looks like sidecars keep opening new outbound connections
samir: on it, running `ss -s` and `netstat -an | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l` now
samir: `TIME_WAIT` count ~ 140k on a single node, ephemeral port range looks depleted
maria: which fleet? dedicated vectorizers or the ephemeral batch workers?
ashley: vectorizers. we rolled a new model version around 02:10 and autoscaler blasted nodes up quickly
jordan: ah — the rollout combined with lambda warmups and a k8s rollout healthcheck spike last night. many short-lived connects to our S3 model store
rachel: any chance this is healthcheck flapping? the readiness probe uses wget to our staging metrics endpoint
samir: it's a mix. also saw lots of concurrent TCP connects to s3.amazonaws.com:443 from port ranges mapping to same NAT IP. NAT ports per IP are ~64k minus some reserved, with AWS SNAT reuse we're hitting collisions
ashley: quick mitigation: can we add an egress proxy (socat/nginx) to multiplex connections or route model pulls through dedicated egress ENIs?
jordan: we spun up a spare NAT gateway in the AZ and attached an EIP to a new ENI — that dropped port utilization by ~30% immediately
maria: nice. can we also tweak kubelet `--hairpin-mode` or container keepalive so pulls reuse connections?
samir: two-pronged: 1) immediate: route model-puller subnets to the spare NAT and add iptables MASQUERADE rotation on the nodes; 2) medium: enable S3 VPC endpoints for model fetches to avoid SNAT completely
atalie-bot: runbook note: when NAT port usage >90% in an AZ, consider adding NAT gateway, enable S3 gateway endpoint, and throttle concurrent model fetches
ashley: logged the runbook changes. also throttled the autoscaler with a `maxSurge` change to reduce concurrent boot storms
rachel: we should also fix the readiness probe to use an internal port to avoid external egress for prod pods
jordan: putting a canary patch that serializes model pulls (backoff + jitter) into the init container now — will push in 5m
samir: for diagnostics, here's the quick check I ran: ```
# aggregate ephemeral usage by nat ip
aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters "Name=description,Values=*nat-3a*" --query 'NetworkInterfaces[*].{ID:NetworkInterfaceId,PrivateIp:PrivateIpAddress}'
# then check CloudWatch NATPortUtilization metric for those ENIs
```
maria: what about port randomization on our sidecars? we can enable SO_REUSEPORT or reuse sockets in the fetcher to reduce churn
ashley: agreed. put a ticket for sidecar keepalive + connection pooling, priority P0 for next sprint
devops-runner: temporary patch deployed: route table for subnet-prod-fetchers -> nat-3b (new natgw), throttled KPA target from 120 to 40 for 10m, and added S3 gateway endpoint in eu-west-1
rachel: errors are dropping, 502 rate down to normal within ~2m :thumbsup:
samir: follow-ups: 1) confirm all AZs have NAT headroom or S3 endpoints, 2) implement client-side pooling in vectorizer image, 3) add CloudWatch alarm for ephemeral port exhaustion (not just overall NAT util)
ashley: adding alarms and a dashboard widget for per-NAT port exhaustion. thanks everyone for the quick ops! :heart:
